segments.title: 第151章 喜歡
segments.content:
Chapter 151: Liking

Ying Chanxi had been acting strange lately.

Her knees and wrists had actually healed a little over a week after the sports meet.

But after she recovered, she started shutting herself in her bedroom all the time.

She stopped eating late-night snacks, would shower as soon as she got home, and then go straight back to her room. On weekends, she would stay in her bedroom all day, only coming out for meals.

No one knew what she was up to.

She wouldn't say even when Li Luo asked.

And during this time, Li Luo didn't really have the energy to worry about other things.

Because *I'm Really Not a Star* had blown up.

From the end of November and for a week after, his new daily subscriptions hovered around 2,000.

Although the numbers began to decline after that, they suddenly surged again in mid-December.

Li Luo went on Weibo to check and immediately understood the reason. His heart turned to ash.

The reason was that Yuan Wanqing, while on an interview show she was invited to, had talked about the creator of the song "Annual Rings."

The show's production team was quite good at digging up information. They uncovered that the lyricist and composer of "Annual Rings," Chong Ran, was a web novel author.

Using this as a topic, they began to chat with Yuan Wanqing.

Yuan Wanqing, of course, wouldn't casually reveal Li Luo's true identity, but she generously and openly stated that she was also reading this author's novel and mentioned that she knew him in real life.

The show was quite popular due to its witty host.

Once this episode aired, its viewership hit a new high.

And just like that, basically everyone who followed *Immortal Fate of the Jade Pool*, Yuan Wanqing, or "Annual Rings" now knew that the song "Annual Rings" was written by a web novel author named Chong Ran.

At this point, Li Luo could only sadly accept this fact and then resolve to avoid going to Yan Zhusheng's house as much as possible in the future.

He didn't know if Yuan Wanqing would actually finish reading his book.

He could only pray in his heart that what Yuan Wanqing said in the interview was just for show. In reality, given her deeper understanding of the entertainment industry's inner workings and actual operations, she should be able to find many bugs in the plot logic of his entertainment-focused novel.

Hopefully, she can't bring herself to finish it…

Holding on to this thought, Li Luo sighed and continued to obediently attend school.

As time moved into late December, the temperature gradually dropped.

During the day in Yuhang City, the highest temperature was only around eight or nine degrees, and at night it dropped to nearly two or three degrees.

Students who were afraid of the cold were already wearing scarves.

"What's this?"

Returning to school on Sunday evening, Li Luo saw Yan Zhusheng walk into the classroom holding a large package and couldn't help but ask curiously.

"For you." Yan Zhusheng stuffed the package into Li Luo's arms and sat down in her own seat.

Li Luo was stunned for a moment, not quite registering. "For me? What is it?"

"A birthday present," Yan Zhusheng said, tilting her head. "Isn't it your birthday today?"

"Huh?" Li Luo secretly pulled out his phone and glanced at the date: December 21st.

Well, it really was his birthday.

It's just that Li Luo hadn't really celebrated his birthday since graduating from elementary school.

If he counted his previous life, it had been over twenty years since he'd received a birthday present from anyone.

Suddenly receiving one out of the blue was actually quite moving.

"How did you know it's my birthday today?" Li Luo asked strangely, holding the package. "I don't think I ever mentioned it."

"It's written on your QQ profile," Yan Zhusheng said, blinking. "It should be correct, right?"

"It's not wrong…"

Although many people would randomly fill in a birthday, Li Luo had properly entered his real one. He just hadn't expected Yan Zhusheng to prepare a birthday gift for him.

"So what did you get me?"

"You can open it and see."

Since Yan Zhusheng said so, Li Luo didn't stand on ceremony any longer and lowered his head to unwrap the package.

Inside was a shoebox.

After opening the lid, he saw a pair of white athletic sneakers inside.

"I saw that your sneakers were a bit old, and we still have to run and work out together, so I thought a new pair would be good," Yan Zhusheng said.

"You know my size?"

"Oh… When I was at your house, I secretly checked the size of your shoes."

"You're pretty clever."

Li Luo snipped off the tag and then looked at Yan Zhusheng. "Should I put them on now?"

"Mhm." Yan Zhusheng nodded, helped him thread the laces through the sneakers, and then placed them by his feet.

Soon, Li Luo had the new shoes on. As he tied one shoelace, Yan Zhusheng knelt by the other side and helped tie the lace there.

After putting them on, Li Luo stood up and walked a couple of steps. They fit perfectly and were more comfortable than his old pair. There was even a slight spring in his step, a clear sign of a high-end product.

"How much did these shoes cost?"

"I don't know." Yan Zhusheng shook her head. "I asked my mom to help me buy them. She said this pair was good quality."

Hearing this, Li Luo felt a little embarrassed and asked in a low voice, "Did your mom say anything after reading my novel?"

"She said you wrote many of the processes too simply, that the real situation is much more complicated." Yan Zhusheng thought for a moment, recalling. "And also that there are too many female leads. One is enough, preferably Mo Qinghan. Get rid of the other two."

"Are you sure the last part was what your auntie said?" Li Luo asked, narrowing his eyes.

Yan Zhusheng blinked and looked down at Li Luo's new shoes. "Do you like the shoes?"

"Yan Zhusheng, you're so smart yet a little dense at the same time."

Yan Zhusheng didn't understand and continued to ask, "Do you like them or not?"

"I like them." Li Luo sat back down in his seat with a laugh. "Thanks for the gift, and please thank your auntie for me too. With her promotion, my book's performance has improved a lot."

"My mom said she's the one who should be thanking you," Yan Zhusheng said seriously.

And that was indeed the case.

Compared to Li Luo who rode this wave of traffic to go from around 4,000 average subscriptions to the current 7,000, Yuan Wanqing had clearly gained much more from this incident.

Not only did she truly return to the public eye, but she also leveraged the single "Annual Rings" to raise her current commercial value.

This was the case for many celebrities.

Often, it wasn't that you lacked talent, but that you lacked a stage and an opportunity to display that talent.

Once an opportunity was seized, traffic would come pouring in, and things that were once out of reach would suddenly become attainable.

In less than a month, Yuan Wanqing had leveraged the boost from "Annual Rings" to achieve a major comeback.

As a result, some of the songs on her new album, which were of good quality themselves, were now being discovered by netizens, and they ended up climbing the music charts along with "Annual Rings."

How could the profits from this be measured in just a few million?

Just the few endorsements that Huayue Film and Television had negotiated for Yuan Wanqing had already easily covered the initial costs, and then some.

In comparison, Li Luo's average subscriptions would probably double by the end of the month.

His royalties would only increase from about 20,000 a month to around 40,000.

"My mom wanted me to tell you something," Yan Zhusheng added. "The contracts for 'The Light Chaser' and 'Light' can be re-signed to give you a price increase."

"There's no need for that." Li Luo shook his head. "A deal that's already been made doesn't need to be overturned. Just because 'Annual Rings' blew up doesn't mean the other songs I write will have the same effect. Your auntie really doesn't need to feel bad about it."

"Then there's one more thing," Yan Zhusheng said again. "Because my mom needs to perform 'Annual Rings' on some stages, like the Qianjiang Province New Year's Eve Gala, they're considering inviting her to perform a song. We'll need to renegotiate the copyright for that."

The copyright agreement Huayue Film and Television had previously signed with Li Luo for "Annual Rings" was primarily for a series of rights related to the TV drama.

Now that "Annual Rings" had become Yuan Wanqing's most representative work, it naturally required authorization for many other types of rights.

Of course, Yuan Wanqing clearly had another intention, which was to give him money as a thank you.

After all, her major comeback was entirely due to Li Luo's song "Annual Rings," yet Li Luo had only received less than 300,000 for his three songs.

This made Yuan Wanqing feel that it wasn't quite right.

After listening to Yan Zhusheng, Li Luo nodded. "Mhm, we can discuss that. But if your auntie needs to use it urgently, she can sing it first. We can sort out the authorization contract later. I'm not in a hurry."

"So, my place next week?" Yan Zhusheng's eyes lit up as she asked.

Hearing this invitation, Li Luo fell silent.

The thought of Yuan Wanqing having read his novel made him hesitant to go to Yan Zhusheng's house now.

"I'll have to think about that…"

"Then I'll have my mom come to your place."

"No, no, no!" Li Luo waved his hands repeatedly. "I'll go, I'll go. It's better if I go to your place."

No more people could find out about his writing!

It was one thing for Yan Zhusheng to know.

If Ying Chanxi and Xu Youyu also found out, living under the same roof every day, Li Luo couldn't even imagine that scene.

"Then it's a deal." Yan Zhusheng finalized the plan, then packed Li Luo's old shoes into the shoebox and placed it aside for him.

Li Luo sighed, feeling like life was getting harder and harder.

(End of Chapter)
